recent_posts.title: Spotify wants to become the home for AI-generated personal audio
recent_posts.summary: Spotify has launched a beta CLI tool that lets users create AI-generated personal podcasts using coding agents like OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code and import them directly into their Spotify library. The podcasts are private and only visible to the creator. Users can write natural language prompts to generate audio content on topics of their choice, then access it alongside their regular Spotify listening.

recent_posts.title: Unknown hackers evict TeamPCP from compromised systems and steal credentials
recent_posts.summary: An unknown hacking group dubbed 'PCPJack' by SentinelOne researchers is targeting systems already compromised by the cybercrime group TeamPCP. After evicting TeamPCP and removing its tools, PCPJack deploys a self-spreading worm across cloud infrastructure, steals credentials, and exfiltrates data. The group also scans for exposed services like Docker and MongoDB. Their motives appear financial — reselling credentials, acting as initial access brokers, or extorting victims directly. SentinelOne researchers are unsure of the group's identity, theorizing they could be ex-TeamPCP members, a rival group, or a third party modeling attacks on TeamPCP's earlier campaigns.

recent_posts.title: How Anthropic’s Mythos has rewritten Firefox’s approach to cybersecurity
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic's new Mythos AI model has dramatically improved Firefox's security posture by uncovering hundreds of high-severity bugs, including sandbox vulnerabilities and decade-old code flaws. Mozilla shipped 423 bug fixes in April 2026 alone, compared to 31 a year prior. Unlike previous AI security tools plagued by false positives, Mythos uses agentic self-assessment to filter results. However, Mozilla still relies on human engineers to write and review patches, as AI-generated fixes aren't directly deployable. The broader security implications remain uncertain — the tools benefit both attackers and defenders, though Mozilla's Brian Grinstead believes the balance tips slightly toward defense.

recent_posts.title: Police arrest SMS blaster crew that sent malicious messages to thousands across Toronto
recent_posts.summary: Toronto police arrested three men and filed 44 charges for operating an SMS blaster device in downtown Toronto — the first known use of such a device in Canada. The scheme, active since November 2025, blasted tens of thousands of devices with phishing text messages designed to steal banking credentials and other login information. The device spoofed cell towers and exploited 2G network weaknesses, was custom-built, and was operated from a moving vehicle. Users can protect themselves by disabling 2G connectivity or enabling Lockdown Mode on Apple devices.

recent_posts.title: Google’s $9.99-per-month AI health coach launches May 19
recent_posts.summary: Google is launching its AI-powered Health Coach on May 19 as part of the Google Health Premium subscription ($9.99/month or $99/year). Powered by Gemini, the coach acts as a personalized fitness coach, sleep expert, and wellness advisor. It uses an onboarding process to tailor guidance based on user goals, routines, equipment, and health records. The service integrates with fitness, sleep, nutrition, and cycle tracking data. Initially available for Fitbit and Pixel Watch users, the Google Health app (rebranded from Fitbit) will be globally available on the same day as the new Fitbit Air launch. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers get access at no extra cost.

recent_posts.title: China’s Moonshot AI raises $2B at $20B valuation as demand for open-source AI skyrockets
recent_posts.summary: Moonshot AI, the Beijing-based lab behind the Kimi series of open-weight LLMs, has raised $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation. The round was led by Meituan's VC arm Long-Z Investment, with participation from Tsinghua Capital, China Mobile, and CPE Yuanfeng. The company has raised $3.9 billion over the past six months, up from a $4.3 billion valuation at end of 2025. Moonshot's annualized recurring revenue surpassed $200 million in April, driven by paid subscriptions and API usage. Its latest model, Kimi K2.6, is currently the second-most used LLM on OpenRouter. The fundraising reflects surging investor appetite for Chinese open-weight AI models, with rivals DeepSeek, Zhipu AI, and MiniMax also attracting major capital or going public.

recent_posts.title: Spotify’s AI DJ now supports French, German, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese
recent_posts.summary: Spotify has expanded its AI DJ feature to support four new languages — French, German, Italian, and Brazilian Portuguese — each with a distinct AI persona (Maia, Ben, Alex, and Dani). The rollout also extends availability to eight new countries, bringing the total to over 75. The AI DJ, which originally provided automated song commentary, has evolved to support voice commands, mood/genre requests, and text-based prompting similar to ChatGPT or Claude.

recent_posts.title: Elon Musk’s lawsuit is putting OpenAI’s safety record under the microscope
recent_posts.summary: A federal court in Oakland heard testimony in Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, with former employees and board members alleging the company's shift toward commercialization compromised its AI safety mission. Former AGI readiness team member Rosie Campbell testified that OpenAI evolved from a research-focused organization to a product-focused one, citing a GPT-4 deployment in India that bypassed the company's Deployment Safety Board. Former board member Tasha McCauley described a pattern of CEO Sam Altman misleading the board, including lying about a board member's intentions and failing to disclose the public launch of ChatGPT. The case centers on whether OpenAI's for-profit transformation violated its founding mission, with broader implications for AI governance and whether internal oversight of powerful AI labs is sufficient without government regulation.

recent_posts.title: India’s first space tech unicorn emerges as Skyroot gears up for orbital launch
recent_posts.summary: Skyroot Aerospace has become India's first space tech unicorn after raising $60 million at a $1.1 billion pre-money valuation. The Hyderabad-based startup, founded by ex-ISRO engineers, is preparing for the maiden orbital launch of its Vikram-1 rocket in June 2026 — the first orbital launch attempt by an Indian private company. The round was co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and GIC, with BlackRock-affiliated debt. Skyroot plans to use the capital to scale manufacturing, increase Vikram-1 launch cadence, and develop Vikram-2, a heavier cryogenic vehicle targeting debut in 2027. India's space economy is projected to grow from $8.4 billion to $44 billion by 2033.

recent_posts.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications close May 27
recent_posts.summary: TechCrunch's Startup Battlefield 200 competition is accepting applications until May 27. Pre-Series A startups can apply for a chance to pitch at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, gain global visibility, receive direct VC feedback, and compete for $100,000 in equity-free funding. Selected startups get exhibit space, all-access passes, press list access, and founder masterclasses. Only 200 startups are selected, with 20 finalists pitching live on the Disrupt Stage.
